en: A kingfisher's sharp beak acts as a natural wedge to pierce water and catch fish.
The rough bark of a narra tree provides enough friction for ants to climb without slipping.
Gravity pulls the water of Maria Cristina Falls downward to spin turbines and generate electricity.
Black magnetite sand on Camiguin beaches is naturally magnetic and easily sticks to iron.
Lightning is a massive, visible spark of static electricity jumping between clouds during a thunderstorm.
Rainbows form when sunlight refracts and reflects inside spherical raindrops after a tropical rainstorm.
Philippine forest bats emit high-pitched sound waves and listen for echoes to catch insects.
Hot springs in Tiwi, Albay, are heated by geothermal energy from hot magma beneath the ground.
A falling coconut gains kinetic energy as gravity pulls it faster toward the ground.
Rubbing dry coconut fronds together creates enough friction and heat to start a small fire.
Villagers use a simple fixed pulley to lift heavy buckets of water from deep wells.
Mountain trails in the Cordilleras act as natural inclined planes to make climbing easier.
